To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the noise levels of amorphous TFTs can be predicted by existing theory, and that the noise in amorphous TFTsat zero gate voltage scales with the leakage current in the same way as the leakage current scales with the TFT area.

the current noise power spectra of hydrogenated amorphouse silicon TFTs can be predicted by existing theories for crystalline MOSFETs in the conducting mode, and in the nonconducting state, the noise is proportional to the square of the leakage current.

the current noise power spectral density in amorphous silicon field‐effect transis­tors (a‐SiFETs) is dominated by the channel noise and that the channel noise in the nonconducting state can be described by the same power‐law relationship between the current noise and the leakage current as in crystalline metal‐ox­ide‐semiconductor field‐effect transitors (MOSFETs).

the development of an integrated optical sensor for the determination of the refractive index of gases.
the development of thin‐film solar cells based on amorphous silicon.

The main takeaway from our work is that
TFTs are not fundamentally noisy devices, and that noise levels can be reduced through the use of low‐resistance contacts and by minimizing the leakage current.
